entities.summary: Harry Walter Legge was an English classical music record producer, most especially associated with EMI. His recordings include many sets later regarded as classics and reissued by EMI as "Great Recordings of the Century". He worked in the recording industry from 1927, combining this with the post of junior music critic of The Manchester Guardian. He was assistant to Sir Thomas Beecham at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, and in World War II played a role in bringing music to the armed forces and civilians. Walter Legge was a composers & musicians from London (1906-06-01, London–1979-03-22). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Walter Legge's work as a record producer and music critic had a significant impact on the development of classical music, with his recordings being reissued by EMI as 'Great Recordings of the Century'. His contributions to bringing music to the armed forces and civilians during World War II also had a notable regional impact.
